title: Ines and the Bell
premise: When Mirabel Marchetti returns to the family farmhouse to bury her twin sister Ines, she finds her childhood imaginary friend — a woman called the Bellringer — waiting on the porch, unchanged after thirty years. The house's last resident, great-aunt Serafina, is dying and must sign over the property, but the deed can only pass if someone completes the bell song's missing last verse without singing along; every Marchetti who has sung it has been taken by the bell tower to keep its clapper company. Mirabel, a stubborn skeptic, must learn the verse from Ines's ghost — who may be her sister or something wearing her sister — while deciding whether loyalty to family means finishing the song or finally breaking it. She ends the inheritance by singing the verse alone in the tower, refusing to let the bell answer, and walks out as the last Marchetti with nothing but the truth.
about_author: Mirabel Villalobos grew up in a coastal village where church bells rang for both weddings and disappearances, a fact she was told never to mention to outsiders. She writes horror about families that mistake silence for love.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Mirabel arrives for the funeral and discovers the headstone reads 'Ines' while everyone insists they buried Mirabel. Third-person limited from Mirabel's POV. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into defiance — she corrects the stone herself and dares anyone to argue.

chapters.title: Someone on the Porch
chapters.summary: At the farmhouse, the Bellringer sits on the porch swing exactly as Mirabel left her at age seven, humming. Mirabel's skepticism holds until the swing moves under no weight. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a childhood comfort turned threat.

chapters.title: Serafina's Terms
chapters.summary: Great-aunt Serafina, lucid only at dusk, explains the deed requires the song's last verse sung by an heir who does not sing along. She shows Mirabel the family ledger of names crossed out by the bell. POV: alternating Mirabel and Serafina. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as legal procedure.

chapters.title: What Ines Kept
chapters.summary: Sorting her sister's room, Mirabel finds sheet music annotated in two handwritings — one hers, one not — and a recording of Ines practicing a verse that stops mid-phrase. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion that Ines knew she would die.

chapters.title: The Bellringer's Version
chapters.summary: The Bellringer offers to teach Mirabel the verse, sweetly, in exchange for being acknowledged as real. Mirabel refuses and the Bellringer begins appearing in mirrors, windows, the funeral photos. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: loneliness weaponized — the friend who punishes abandonment.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Taken
chapters.summary: Mirabel researches the parish records: every heir who completed the verse vanished the same night, and each disappearance coincided with a bell rung by no one. A neighbor, old Tomas, admits he heard his brother in the tower for years. POV: third person shifting between Mirabel and Tomas. Emotional beat: the horror of corroborated folklore.

chapters.title: Serafina Signs
chapters.summary: Weakened and frightened, Serafina signs the papers early to force Mirabel's hand before she flees. That night the Bellringer sings the first three verses flawlessly, and the tower answers. POV: Serafina, then Mirabel. Emotional beat: betrayal by love — family pushing her toward the altar of inheritance.

chapters.title: Ines, Unchanged
chapters.summary: Ines appears at the foot of Mirabel's bed, offering the true last verse but warning that hearing it fully means wanting to sing it. Mirabel must decide whether this ghost is her sister or the bell wearing her. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh — which sibling is she loyal to?

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Climax. Mirabel climbs the tower at dawn, learns the verse note by note from Ines, and sings it alone while the Bellringer harmonizes, trying to make her sing along. The bell swings toward her voice; Mirabel finishes and falls silent, refusing the answering note. The bell cracks. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into will.

chapters.title: No Heir Remaining
chapters.summary: Resolution. The house stands empty and unsellable; Serafina dies at peace; the Bellringer fades from the porch, unacknowledged at last. Mirabel buries the ledger, keeps only Ines's half-written page, and leaves town without looking back. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: costly belonging — she ends the line to keep herself.
